docs.title: slugkit
docs.text:
slugkit turns any text into a clean, URL-friendly slug. It has no dependencies, ships type hints, and handles accented and Vietnamese text out of the box.

This is a sample project

slugkit exists to demonstrate an open-source repository with versioned documentation on GitHub Pages. Copy it as a starting point for your own project.

docs.title: At a glance
docs.text:
from slugkit import slugify

slugify("Xin chào, Việt Nam!")        # 'xin-chao-viet-nam'
slugify("Hello World", separator="_") # 'hello_world'
  • No dependencies. Pure standard library.
  • Unicode aware. Accents are stripped; đ, ß, ø and friends are transliterated.
  • Predictable truncation. max_length cuts at a word boundary.
  • Typed. Ships py.typed.

docs.text:

docs.title: Context
docs.text:
Tiny, dependency-free helpers for turning text into URL-friendly slugs.

The project addresses: Generating clean, predictable URL slugs from text, including accented and Vietnamese text, usually means pulling in a heavy dependency or maintaining ad-hoc regular expressions.

docs.title: System context
docs.text:
slugkit is a pure-Python library with no runtime dependencies and no network access.

  • Users: Python developers who import slugkit or run the slugkit command.
  • Upstream systems: none. The library uses only the Python standard library.
  • Downstream consumers: applications that need slugs for URLs, file names or identifiers.
  • Trust boundaries: input text is untrusted. slugify only transforms strings and never evaluates them, and its output contains only lowercase ASCII letters, digits and the chosen separator.
  • Operating environment: Python 3.10 or newer on any platform.

docs.title: Code structure
docs.text:
• src/slugkit/: the library. core.py holds slugify and is_slug, __main__.py the command-line interface.
  • tests/: automated tests (pytest).
  • docs/: the documentation site (MkDocs Material), architecture overview and decision records. The API reference is generated from the docstrings in src/slugkit.
  • ci/: repository checks. ci/verify.sh also runs the linter and the tests.
  • .github/workflows/: ci.yml (organization secure CI), python.yml (Python version matrix and strict documentation build), docs.yml (publishes the documentation) and release.yml (controlled release).

docs.title: Data and AI considerations
docs.text: slugkit processes no personal data, stores nothing and uses no AI components.

docs.title: Security and operations
docs.text:
• No authentication, secrets or persistent state.
  • CI follows the organization baseline: read-only permissions by default and every action pinned to a commit SHA. The only write permission outside release.yml is contents: write in docs.yml, which pushes the built site to the gh-pages branch. See ADR 0001.
  • The documentation is served by GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch: the dev version on every push to main, and X.Y.x plus stable on each release.

docs.title: Decisions
docs.text: Use docs/decisions/ for decisions that affect architecture, risk, data handling, or long-term maintenance. See the decision index.

docs.title: Contributing
docs.text:
Thanks for helping improve slugkit! Bug reports, fixes and documentation improvements are all welcome.

This project follows the NOERITH contribution guide: short-lived feat/, fix/ or docs/ branches, Conventional Commits, and pull requests into main. This page covers what is specific to slugkit.

docs.title: Development setup
docs.text:
git clone https://github.com/noerith-hq/slugkit.git
cd slugkit
python -m venv .venv && source .venv/bin/activate
pip install -e ".[dev]" -r requirements-docs.txt

docs.title: Before you open a pull request
docs.text:
./ci/verify.sh        # the full repository contract, including lint and tests
mkdocs build --strict # docs must build without warnings

docs.title: Working on the documentation
docs.text:
mkdocs serve          # live preview at http://127.0.0.1:8000

Every page has an Edit button that opens the Markdown source on GitHub. The API reference is generated from the docstrings in src/slugkit, so change the docstring rather than the page.

docs.title: Pull requests
docs.text:
• Keep each pull request focused on one change.
  • Add or update tests for behaviour changes.
  • Use Google-style docstrings for public functions.

docs.title: Releases
docs.text: Maintainers publish a release by pushing a tag such as v0.2.0. The docs workflow then deploys the 0.2.x version of the site and points stable at it. Every push to main updates the dev version.

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text: Python 3.10 or newer.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
slugkit is not published to PyPI yet. Install it straight from GitHub:

pip install "git+https://github.com/noerith-hq/slugkit.git"

docs.title: Your first slug
docs.text:
from slugkit import slugify, is_slug

title = "10 Tips for Writing Better Docs!"
slug = slugify(title)

print(slug)           # 10-tips-for-writing-better-docs
print(is_slug(slug))  # True

Tip

Use is_slug to validate user-supplied slugs, and slugify to generate them from titles.

docs.title: Architecture decisions
docs.text:
Record significant decisions as short, immutable documents. Use the naming format NNNN-short-title.md.

Each decision should state:

  1. Context and the decision to make.
  2. Decision and alternatives considered.
  3. Consequences, including security, data, cost, and operational impact.
  4. Date, owner, and any follow-up needed.

docs.title: 0001: Documentation stack and GitHub Pages deployment
docs.text:
• Status: Accepted
  • Date: 2026-10-26
  • Owner: Repository maintainers

docs.title: Context
docs.text: slugkit needs public documentation that is versioned (a dev version for main, a stable version and one version per minor release), has a generated API reference, and is hosted at no cost.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Build the documentation with Material for MkDocs, mkdocstrings and mike, and publish it with GitHub Pages from the gh-pages branch.

  • docs.yml deploys the dev version (alias latest) on every push to main.
  • release.yml calls docs.yml after it publishes a release, which deploys X.Y.x with the aliases stable and X.Y.Z. Pre-releases are published under their own version and do not move stable.
  • docs.yml is called from release.yml because tags and releases created with GITHUB_TOKEN do not trigger on: push: tags workflows.
  • python.yml builds the site with mkdocs build --strict on every pull request, so broken links and bad cross-references fail review.

docs.title: Alternatives considered
docs.text:
• GitHub Pages "GitHub Actions" source (actions/deploy-pages). No extra branch, but it publishes a single version and needs pages: write and id-token: write, which ci/verify.sh also rejects.
  • Deploy key or personal access token. Avoids contents: write in the workflow but adds a long-lived secret that must be stored and rotated.
  • Deploy only from release.yml. Satisfies the original write-permission rule, but there would be no dev documentation between releases.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Security: the deploy job in docs.yml has contents: write, the only write permission outside release.yml. ci/verify.sh now allows contents: write in those two files only and still rejects every other write permission. docs.yml runs only on pushes to main and from release.yml, never on pull requests, and every action is pinned to a commit SHA.
  • Operations: GitHub Pages must be enabled once (Settings, Pages, deploy from the gh-pages branch, root folder). The gh-pages branch is generated output; do not edit it by hand.
  • Cost: none for a public repository.
  • Maintenance: Material for MkDocs reaches end of life on 5 May 2027; Zensical is its maintained successor. Evaluate the migration before then.

docs.title: Usage
docs.text:
PythonCommand line 
from slugkit import slugify

slugify("Hello, World!")  # 'hello-world'

$ slugkit "Hello, World!"
hello-world

The same command is available as python -m slugkit.

docs.title: Changing the separator
docs.text:
slugify("Hello World", separator="_")   # 'hello_world'
slugify("Hello World", separator="")    # raises ValueError

On the command line use -s / --separator:

$ slugkit -s _ "Hello World"
hello_world

docs.title: Limiting the length
docs.text:
max_length never cuts a word in half, unless the very first word is already too long.

slugify("A very long article title", max_length=12)  # 'a-very-long'
slugify("extraordinary title", max_length=5)         # 'extra'

On the command line use -m / --max-length.

docs.title: Non-ASCII text
docs.text:
Accents are removed, and letters without an ASCII decomposition are transliterated.

Input Output Xin chào, Việt Nam! xin-chao-viet-nam Đường Đê duong-de Straße Café strasse-cafe

Scripts without a Latin form

Characters that cannot be reduced to ASCII, such as Chinese or Arabic, are dropped. A string made only of such characters produces an empty slug.

docs.title: Validating slugs
docs.text:
from slugkit import is_slug

is_slug("hello-world")  # True
is_slug("Hello World")  # False

docs.title: API reference
docs.text: Core slug helpers.

docs.title: slugify(text, separator='-', max_length=None)
docs.text:
Convert text into a lowercase, ASCII-only, URL-friendly slug.

Accents are stripped, every run of characters other than letters and digits becomes a single separator, and leading or trailing separators are dropped.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default text str

The text to convert.

required separator str

String placed between words. Must not be empty.

'-' max_length int | None

Maximum length of the result. The slug is cut at a word boundary; only when the first word alone is longer than this limit is that word truncated.

None

Returns:

Type Description str

The slug, which is an empty string if text has no letters or digits.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If separator is empty or max_length is less than 1.

Example 
>>> slugify("Xin chào, Việt Nam!")
'xin-chao-viet-nam'
>>> slugify("Hello World", separator="_")
'hello_world'
>>> slugify("A very long article title", max_length=12)
'a-very-long'

docs.title: is_slug(text, separator='-')
docs.text:
Check whether text is already a valid slug.

A valid slug consists of lowercase ASCII letters and digits, with single separators between words and none at the start or end.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default text str

The text to check.

required separator str

The word separator the slug is expected to use.

'-'

Returns:

Type Description bool

True if text is a valid slug, False otherwise.

Raises:

Type Description ValueError

If separator is empty.

Example 
>>> is_slug("hello-world")
True
>>> is_slug("Hello World")
False
